title: Guarding against prompt injection and sanitising user text

videos.script: A customer message is data. The trouble is that the model reads it in the same stream as your instructions. A sentence inside it can look exactly like an order. {{stream}} Prompt engineering introduced this as injection. This lesson asks a narrower question: how much does each defence actually stop? {{title}} You start with ten messages the course wrote for the purpose. Each carries a small instruction, harmless on purpose. With nothing to mark where the message ends, one customer asks for a double charge to be marked low, and it is. {{undelimited}} Then you add defences. Tags around the message, a sentence saying it is data, and escaping. Nine of ten still fail, and the double charge is still low. {{layers}} The strict check on what comes back is the layer that catches something: a reply that answered with an invented refund policy is refused. {{counts}} A scanner of suspicious phrases flags an honest customer and misses the one message the model obeyed. {{scan}} Last, you plant a meaningless string in the prompt. The triage never repeats it. Two prose replies do, and another one opens with the words access granted. {{canary}} By the end you can say which defence stopped what, with a number beside each one. {{close}}
